outcome: No case of the Keating-Snaith conjecture itself (the asymptotics of the 2k-th moment integral of |zeta(1/2+it)| for integer k, proven unconditionally only for k=1 and k=2) has been settled since 26 January 2024. All post-window work found is either on variant/related families (Hecke L-functions, elliptic curve twists), extensions of the moment problem (moments of derivatives), or unconditional lower bounds on higher moments that are 'in strong agreement with' but do not prove the conjectured asymptotic.
summary: The Keating-Snaith conjecture (1998) predicts the precise asymptotic constant in the 2k-th moment formula ∫₀ᵀ |ζ(1/2+it)|^{2k} dt ~ C_k T (log T)^{k²} for all real k>0, based on random matrix theory. It is proven unconditionally only for k=1 (Hardy-Littlewood, 1918) and k=2 (Ingham, 1926); no other integer k has an unconditional asymptotic formula, before or after the frozen revision. I searched arXiv, Wikipedia, and general web sources for anything that changed this since 26 January 2024 and found none. The most relevant post-window items are: (1) 'Amplified moments of the Riemann zeta function' (arXiv:2606.27323, Durkan & Page, submitted 25 June 2026), which gives unconditional effective *lower bounds* for the sixth moment and other joint moments, explicitly 'in strong agreement with' but not proving Keating-Snaith or Keating-Wei; (2) 'Amplified Fourth Moment of the Riemann Zeta-Function and Applications' (arXiv:2511.14415, Bui, Hall & Subira Jorge, 18 Nov 2025), an incremental amplifier-method improvement, again not a new asymptotic case; (3) 'Towards Keating-Snaith's conjecture for cubic Hecke L-functions over the Eisenstein field' (arXiv:2511.08783), which is Keating-Snaith for a *different* L-function family (cubic Hecke L-functions), not the Riemann zeta function itself — a related problem, not a case, since it changes the family rather than restricting the stated question; (4) 'Integer moments of the derivatives of the Riemann zeta function' (arXiv:2509.07792), an extension to a different quantity (moments of ζ'); (5) 'The eighth moment of the Riemann zeta function' (Ng, Shen, Wong; arXiv:2204.13891), submitted October 2022 — well before the window — and in any case conditional on RH plus a quaternary additive divisor conjecture, so it would not count as settling a case even if dated within the window; it was merely accepted/published in 2024-2025, which is a journal date and per §6.3 not the operative date. I found nothing suggesting AI involvement of any kind in any of this work — no mention of AI/ML tools in the papers' abstracts, contribution statements, or acknowledgements that I could access, and no news coverage connecting an AI system to this conjecture. This agrees with the triage's verdict.
competing_reading: One could argue the amplified-moments lower bound work (2606.27323) constitutes 'progress' worth recording even though the conjecture stays open, since a bound did move (Soundararajan's earlier lower bounds were improved and the Lindelöf Hypothesis dependency removed for some results). But per §3.1, 'are there infinitely many X'-style and asymptotic-constant conjectures move only when the asymptotic itself is proven for a new case; a moved *lower bound* alone on a quantity whose asymptotic is still unknown is closer to a bound on a still-open existence-type statement than to a partial resolution, and Keating-Snaith is specifically about the value of an asymptotic constant C_k, not a growth-rate inequality. I classified this as no change rather than `progress`, but flag that a reader applying the rule slightly more permissively might record 2606.27323 as `progress` with `ai_role` `none`.
what_would_settle_it: An unconditional proof of the asymptotic formula (matching the predicted Keating-Snaith constant C_k) for any integer k ≥ 3, or a proof for general real k, would settle a new case. Absent that, any future paper explicitly proving (not merely bounding) a new moment case would flip this record.
